Analysis: Both hypotheses propose innovative combinations of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated survivin targeting and immune checkpoint blockade in HCC, but Hypothesis 2 offers a slightly more refined approach. It emphasizes hepatocyte-specific nanoparticle systems and in situ suppression, which may enhance targeting accuracy and reduce off-target effects. Moreover, its framework addresses the timing and kinetics of synergy with PD-1 blockade more explicitly, making it potentially more testable and better suited for dissecting immunogenic cell death pathways. While both approaches face similar challenges with delivery and off-target safety, Hypothesis 2’s focus on hepatocyte-specific delivery and detailed immunogenic readouts appears to strengthen its overall plausibility and safety profile.
